answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the protocol kernel enforces quadratic stake burning for concurrent identity creation, turning the network into a defensive reef against automated clones. Each new participant must burn cryptographic capital proportional to total active aliases, ensuring superlinear cost scaling: registering n identities requires O(n²) burned collateral. Any hollow echo of duplicated activity becomes exponentially unprofitable, exhausting adversary resources while legitimate solo agents thrive.
